sources.entry: Piwigo - Photo gallery software for the web, built by an active community of users and developers. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP
Piwigo | Photo gallery software for the web

summary.one_liner: Piwigo is open source photo gallery and photo library management software for the web, designed for organisations, teams and individuals.
summary.what_it_does: Piwigo is described as photo gallery software for the web for managing a photo library. The README points to piwigo.org for the feature list, demos, forums, documentation and examples. It lists its requirements as a web server (Apache or nginx recommended), PHP 7.4+, MySQL 5+ or MariaDB, and ImageMagick (recommended) or PHP GD. Installation is described as a manual upload of the unzipped release to a web space followed by a browser setup, or via Docker using a separate guide. The README does not detail specific features beyond the general description. Contributions are taken as forks with changes submitted to the master branch.
use_cases: host a photo gallery on your own website
manage a large personal or team photo library
share photo albums on the web
self-host an online photo gallery with PHP and MySQL
how_to_run: Ensure a web server, PHP 7.4+, MySQL 5+ or MariaDB, and ImageMagick or PHP GD are available
Download the latest stable version of Piwigo and unzip it
Transfer all files to your web space with an FTP client
Open your website in a browser and follow the setup steps
For Docker, follow the installation guide linked in the README
notable: Designed for organisations, teams and individuals
Community-driven open source project under GPL v2
Docker installation option described in the README
Piwigo Cloud hosted option mentioned for users without their own server
caveats: Requires PHP 7.4+ (older PHP 7.0 versions are end-of-life and not maintained)
Needs a web server plus a MySQL or MariaDB database
README gives little detail on specific features; see piwigo.org for those
